text: gmx make_ndx builds GROMACS index (.ndx) groups interactively or from commands. Syntax in myrmidon gmx_make_ndx commands: group names containing non-alphanumeric characters must be quoted in double quotes, group numbers are bare integers, boolean operators are '|' (OR / union), '&' (AND / intersection), and '!' (NOT / negation). Atom-name selection uses 'a' (e.g. '0 & ! a H*' selects all non-hydrogen heavy atoms of group 0, useful on a single-ligand coordinate file so atoms are numbered from 1). Residue-name selection uses 'r' (e.g. 'r JZ4'). To merge a protein and a bound ligand into one temperature-coupling bath (so a small ligand is never coupled to its own thermostat), use command '"Protein" | "Other"' or '"Protein" | "JZ4"', producing group Protein_Other alongside Water_and_ions.

gmx mindist computes the minimum distance between two groups of atoms and the number of contacts within a cutoff distance (-d, default 0.6 nm) over a trajectory. Options: -f trajectory (.xtc/.trr), -s structure/tpr, -n index (.ndx), -od minimum distance vs time (.xvg), -on number of contacts vs time (.xvg), -or minimum distance per residue (-respertime writes per-residue distance matrix over time), -d contact cutoff in nm, -group count contacts with multiple atoms in the second group as one contact. In myrmidon, use traj_analyze with metric='mindist' (reports mean, min, largest and final distance) or metric='contacts' (reports per-residue contact fraction over the trajectory in both topology and deposited PDB numbering).

gmx select writes dynamic or static atom/residue selections using GROMACS selection syntax (distinct from traditional make_ndx prompt syntax). Syntax examples: 'resname JZ4 and not name "H*"', 'group "Protein" and within 0.4 of resname JZ4', 'backbone', 'resid 1 to 100'. Note: for trajectory analysis in myrmidon, traj_analyze uses MDAnalysis selection syntax ('protein and backbone', 'resname JZ4 and not name H*', 'resid 42'), NOT make_ndx ('0 & ! a H*') and NOT the keyword 'heavy'.

gmx genrestr produces an #include position-restraint file (posre.itp) for a single moleculetype from a coordinate file (-f) and an index group (-n), with force constants -fc (default 1000 1000 1000 kJ mol^-1 nm^-2). CRITICAL: atom indices in [ position_restraints ] are 1-based WITHIN THE MOLECULETYPE, not global system atom numbers. Always run gmx_make_ndx and gmx_genrestr on the isolated ligand structure (e.g. JZ4_GMX.gro where atoms are numbered 1..N_lig) before complex_assemble, never on the assembled complex.

gmx pdb2gmx reads a coordinate file (.pdb/.gro), matches residues against the chosen force field's residue database (.rtp), adds hydrogens, writes the GROMACS topology (.top) and position restraints (posre.itp). Options: -ff force field (e.g. amber99sb-ildn, charmm36-jul2022), -water water model (tip3p, spce, tip4p), -ignh ignore input hydrogens and rebuild according to force field rules. Non-polymer HETATM records (ligands, buffer ions, crystal waters) not in the force field .rtp must be split out with structure_select before running gmx_pdb2gmx; kept structural ions/waters go after TER in their own chains. Note that .gro output renumbers residues sequentially from 1 and drops PDB insertion codes.

gmx editconf converts coordinate formats and defines the periodic simulation box around a solute. Options: -bt box type (cubic, triclinic, dodecahedron, octahedron), -d distance from the solute to the box wall in nm (minimum periodic image distance is 2*d; keep d >= 1.0 nm so the solute cannot see its periodic image across a 1.0-1.2 nm non-bonded cutoff), -c center the solute in the box.

gmx solvate fills the simulation box (-cp boxed.gro) with solvent configurations (-cs spc216.gro) and updates the [ molecules ] section of the topology (-p topol.top) with the number of SOL molecules added. Refuses if the topology is already solvated.

gmx genion replaces solvent molecules with monoatomic ions (e.g. NA, CL) to neutralise the system's net charge (-neutral) and/or reach a target salt concentration (-conc, in mol/L). Requires a run input (.tpr) built by grompp from the solvated coordinates and topology, and updates [ molecules ] in the topology.

gmx grompp (the GROMACS preprocessor) reads a molecular topology (-p .top), coordinates (-c .gro), position-restraint reference coordinates (-r .gro, required whenever define activates -DPOSRES or -DPOSRES_LIG), an index file (-n .ndx), and run parameters (-f .mdp) to compile a portable binary run input (-o .tpr). For MiMiC QM/MM, grompp zeroes MM charges on QMMM-grps, excludes QM-QM LJ interactions, and removes QM-QM bonds.

gmx mdrun performs energy minimisation, molecular dynamics, or trajectory rerun from a compiled .tpr file (-s/-deffnm). Continuation from a checkpoint uses -cpi state.cpt (in myrmidon, use checkpoint_continue so stage directory and deffnm match the checkpoint record).

gmx energy extracts energy, temperature, pressure, volume, density and box terms from a binary .edr file. Term names must match the exact labels in the .edr (e.g. 'Potential', 'Temperature', 'Pressure', 'Density', 'Total-Energy', 'Kinetic-En.').

section: selection grammars: MDAnalysis vs gmx make_ndx vs MiMiCPy prepqm
text:
Myrmidon tools use three distinct atom-selection grammars — never mix them:
1. traj_analyze (MDAnalysis selection grammar):
   - Protein backbone: 'protein and backbone'
   - Ligand heavy atoms: 'resname JZ4 and not name H*' (NEVER use 'heavy' — 'heavy' is not a valid MDAnalysis token)
   - All ligand atoms: 'resname JZ4'
   - Protein heavy atoms: 'protein and not name H*'
   - Specific residues: 'resid 42:50 and protein' (uses topology 1-based residue numbers from .gro/.tpr; check structure_select or system_inspect residue_map when the deposited PDB has offset numbering or insertion codes).
2. gmx_make_ndx (GROMACS make_ndx interactive prompt grammar):
   - Merge protein and ligand bath: '"Protein" | "Other"' (double quotes around group names, '|' for union, '&' for intersection, '!' for negation)
   - Heavy atoms of group 0: '0 & ! a H*'
   - Residue by name: 'r JZ4'.
3. qm_region (MiMiCPy prepqm selection grammar):
   - Commands start with 'add ', 'add-bound ', 'delete ', or 'clear'
   - Clauses use 'FIELD is VALUE' joined by 'and'/'or': e.g. 'add resname is ACT', 'add resid is 42 and name is OG', 'add-bound resid is 42 and name is CB'.
